findings.text: Older versions unaffected: 'Ask ChatGPT' and 'Message' stay in both allowlists, kind logic unchanged (only 'Message' is .dots), and for non-dots the placeholder is now composer.label, which is 'Ask ChatGPT' whenever that label matched, so old behaviour is identical. Because composer.label can only be one of the two allowlisted non-dots labels, the placeholder string is never attacker/user-controlled.

Draft-safety holds. Empty is inferred only when BOTH (a) a descendant with class 'placeholder' exists AND (b) value is exactly the label or label+'\n' (case/whitespace exact, no trimming). A user who types 'Do anything' removes the placeholder node, so the value goes through paragraphDraft and is preserved. Residual theoretical risk is only if ChatGPT left a placeholder node while real text equals the label; that was equally true for 'Ask ChatGPT' and is not new.

'Do anything' is a generic label. Fail-safe if it appears on a second AXTextArea inside the conversation panel: fields.count != 1 throws 'ambiguous, draft preserved' rather than picking one. The same label is added to the DesktopAccessibility.swift:201 focus guard, which only widens which focused editors are accepted for .chatgpt/.dots; the existing stale-focus rejection test was extended to cover it.

No missed matches of the old placeholder in production code. DesktopAppConversation.swift:190 is another app's placeholders. Other 'Ask ChatGPT' occurrences are test fixtures/docs.
